deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building an axiomatic 'tame topology'. A system M_* = (M_I), indexed by finite sets I, gives for each I a family M_I of subsets of R^I (the 'tame parts'). The axioms M1-M4 (and later M5: R in M_1) are stated on earlier pages. They are close to the axioms of a first-order structure or an o-minimal structure: stability under intersection, products and coordinate maps/projections.

Top of page, continuing section 5 of the previous page (examples, excluding the degenerate cases M_n = empty for all n and M_n = {empty set} for all n):
(a) M_n = subsets of R^n of cardinality at most 1.
(b) M_n = finite subsets of R^n.
(c) M_n = all subsets of R^n.
He remarks that none of these examples is interesting 'for us'. The crossed-out marginalia seem to say they are excluded by a further condition, presumably a non-discreteness or richness condition. The top-right margin note reads roughly 'examples b), c) ... à exclure par (2)'.

Section II, 'espaces modérés': parts in M_I are the tame parts of R^I. Points x with {x} in M_1 (the set R_0 of the previous page) are the 'tame points' of R, and likewise of R^d.

Definition. Let A be in M_I, B in M_J and f: A -> B a map. The graph Γ_f lies in A×B, inside R^I×R^J ≅ R^{I⊔J}. The map f is called tame (modéré) if Γ_f is in M_{I⊔J}.

Proposition M2.
- (a) id_A is tame (its graph is the diagonal intersected with A×A).
- (b) Composites of tame maps are tame. The graph of gf is the projection of (Γ_f × C) ∩ (A × Γ_g) along the B-coordinates.
- (c) The inverse of a tame bijection is tame (its graph is the image of Γ_f under a coordinate permutation).

This yields a category Mod_{M_*}. Its objects are pairs (I, A) with A in M_I; its morphisms are tame maps. The forgetful functor (I,A) ↦ A to (Ens) is faithful and conservative.

Margin note: the degenerate case R = {e} is not excluded.

He then defines an equivalent category Esp_{M_*} of tame 'spaces' X with an underlying set |X|. Its forgetful functor X ↦ |X| is faithful, conservative and 'transportable': any bijection |X| ≅ E lifts uniquely to an isomorphism X -> Y (transport of structure, completed on the next page). The next page proves that finite limits exist and are preserved by |·|, and introduces axiom M5: R in M_1.

In modern terms, this is the category of definable sets and definable maps of a structure. It is replaced by an abstract, 'Bourbaki-style' category of tame spaces whose underlying-set functor is uniquely transportable.
errors: The proofs of (a)-(c) are not written. They require the earlier axioms: diagonals and coordinate permutations are tame, stability under products and intersections, and above all stability under projection (existential quantification). Without a projection axiom, (b) fails. Presumably M1-M4 contain these, but this cannot be checked from this page.

Example (a) (cardinality at most 1) must be checked against all of the axioms, e.g. stability under finite unions or complements if those are among them. If complements are required, (a) and (b) fail them. It is unclear which axioms these examples are meant to satisfy; the margin says some are excluded by a condition (2).

ideas.what: Axiomatic system of 'tame' subsets of R^I for finite I, with trivial examples (singletons, finite sets, all sets) to be excluded
ideas.modern_name: Structure on R / o-minimal structure (van den Dries axioms for a 'structure' as a sequence of Boolean algebras S_n)
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (1984 onward), Pillay-Steinhorn (1986), Knight-Pillay-Steinhorn; Tarski for the semialgebraic case
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 'Réflexions sur la topologie modérée' (program only, no axioms written out)

ideas.what: A map between tame sets is tame iff its graph is tame; identities, composites and inverses of bijections are tame, giving a category with a faithful conservative forgetful functor
ideas.modern_name: Category of definable sets and definable maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in model theory / o-minimality (van den Dries, 'Tame topology and o-minimal structures', 1998)

ideas.what: 'Tame points' of R: x with {x} tame (R_0)
ideas.modern_name: Definable closure of the empty set, dcl(∅)

ideas.what: Replacing Mod_{M_*} by an equivalent category Esp_{M_*} of abstract tame spaces whose underlying-set functor is faithful, conservative and uniquely 'transportable'
ideas.modern_name: Uniquely transportable (amnestic, iso-lifting) concrete category; Bourbaki transport of structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bourbaki (espèces de structure); Adámek-Herrlich-Strecker for 'uniquely transportable'

missed.claim: This is a dated, concrete record (from c. 1973-78 onward) of Grothendieck independently axiomatizing tame geometry. He works with tame subsets of R^I, defines tame maps by graphs, and forms an abstract category of tame spaces. This plausibly predates or is contemporaneous with the van den Dries / Pillay-Steinhorn axiomatization of o-minimality, whereas only the brief 1984 Esquisse sketch is usually cited. The mathematics on this page itself is routine.
missed.quote: On dit que f est modéré si Γ_f ∈ M_{I⊔J}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and context for the origins of o-minimality / tame topology. It shows Grothendieck moved early to a categorical framework (Esp_M, transportable forgetful functor) rather than a model-theoretic one.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (definable maps via graphs, category of definable sets, transport of structure) is standard. Its interest is historical: it documents Grothendieck's own axiomatics for tame topology beyond the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Top-right marginal note likely reads 'les exemples b), c) ... à exclure par (2)' rather than 's'excluent de (2)'; the 'images' insertions in b) and c) are uncertain readings.
'(... "oubli")' under the forgetful functor is likely '(= "oubli")'.
Left-margin note near the forgetful functor reads approximately 'on n'exclut pas les modèles de R = {e}, évidemment ... pas intéressant'.
Line 'parties modérées de R^I, points modérés de R, de R^d' is in the main text, not marginalia.
